title: midsprint-curio-notebook-llm-cost-latency-ideas
content:
Mid-sprint brain dump / lab notebook: trying to capture quick reads, tiny experiments, and intuition sketches related to reducing per-token cost without blowing latency SLOs. This is messy on purpose — notes-to-self and a sketchpad for follow-ups.

Context: running short burst of experiments on medium traffic routes (40–200 rps) with 8k avg context. Dedicated pool (g5x2-ish) — want to reduce token cost via batching, cache, and light quantization while keeping P95 latency < 120ms for interactive routes.

Recent reading highlights (quick takeaways):
- "Adaptive Batching for Small GPUs" (paper, arXiv) — idea: dynamic batch-size controller that accounts for prompt length distribution. Good takeaway: controller that optimizes for token-bound horizon (estimated tokens in next 50ms) vs fixed window. Might be useful for our hosted-api low-tier pools.
- "KV-cache eviction: recency vs importance" (conference poster) — simple recency is cheap, but a small LRU+LRU-sampled importance score (attention salience proxy) gave ~6% improvement in hit rate on long sessions. Could integrate as a lightweight filter before eviction.
- Blog: "Prefetching next-token KV for streaming clients" — speculative prefetch helps when network jitter dominates, but hurts when model compute variable; safe only with conservative thresholds.

Open experiments to run (prioritized):
1) Microcontroller: adaptive-batch controller prototype
   - Implement at routing layer a token-horizon estimator: sample previous 200 requests, compute expected remaining decode tokens.
   - Controller chooses small batching-window (5–20ms) adjustable per route.
   - Metric: tokens/sec per GPU, P95 latency, tail queuing (saturated slot).
   - Quick test: route 'chat-small' for 24h, A/B compare vs fixed 10ms batching.
   - Risks: amplifier for long prompts causing queueing; need safety cap per-request.

2) KV-cache eviction probe (cheap importance heuristic)
   - Add sampling hook that computes per-kv-block avg attention during warm-up (first 32 tokens). Use moving average to score blocks.
   - Evict lowest-scoring blocks first; compare to pure-LRU baseline on long multi-turn traces.
   - Evaluation dataset: 500 long sessions from beta customers (anonymized).

3) Tiny quantization pilot on warm path (8-bit fp quant for FFN weights)
   - Build a canary model variant with Q8 FFNs for small routes; restrict to non-sensitive tenants. Measure quality with existing eval prompt set for rollouts.
   - Track generation divergence and cost savings.

Notes on instrumentation and pitfalls:
- Need per-token timing at slot granularity (not just request-level) to understand where latency accumulates: kernel time vs batching wait vs scheduling.
- Resource-tagging: add route-level tags so we can segment cost accounting by batching policy.
- Fallthrough policy: if controller queues > X ms, bypass batching for that request (preserve latency SLO).

Ideas / hypotheses (quick):
- Hypothesis A: modest adaptive batching (10–15% more tokens/GPU) with proper caps will keep P95 within 5% of baseline but reduce cost.
- Hypothesis B: small importance-weighted eviction increases effective cache hit rate on long sessions by 4–8% with negligible CPU overhead.
- Hypothesis C: Q8-FFN yields ~15% speedup on CUDA kernels for medium sequence lengths but may introduce edge-case hallucination regressions on certain prompts — need targeted evals.

Links / quick refs to check:
- arXiv:2602.01234 (adaptive batching paper)
- GH: redwood/inference#8745 — PR with preliminary batching controller prototype (WIP)
- Confluence draft: /display/INF/kv-cache-eviction (contains past experiments, need to reconcile metrics)
- Slack: #inference-experiments thread (search "prefetch jitter" 2026-08)

Small implementation sketch (pseudo):
- Controller loop:
  sample N recent requests -> estimate token_horizon
  target_batch_ms = clamp(base_ms * f(token_horizon), min_ms, max_ms)
  collect requests until target_batch_ms or max_batch_size then dispatch

- Eviction hook:
  on attention step: accumulate salience per-kv-block (sum attention weights over block tokens) with decay lambda
  score = recency_score * alpha + salience_score * (1-alpha)
  evict lowest score first when needed

Todo (next 2 weeks):
- [ ] Wire up per-token timing metrics to tracing pipeline (SRE help: @Arun Patel)
- [ ] Create A/B plan for adaptive batching on stage cluster (target: 2 week ramp)
- [ ] Run offline simulation of eviction heuristic on 1M tokens of session traces (Zara to share anonymized trace)
- [ ] Make small quant canary and run quality evals on existing prompt set

Questions to resolve / discussion prompts for next sync:
- How conservative should bypass thresholds be? (50ms? 100ms?) Prefer route-specific tuning.
- Do we accept small quality regressions for low-tier cost tier? Need product input.
- Ops: what alerting for controller misbehavior? (sustained queue growth, degraded GPU utilization)

Random observations from running quick smoke tests: 
- When we increase max_batch_size from 32 -> 64 on a particular slot type, GPU utilization improved but P99 increased sharply on heavy prompt tails. Suggests more aggressive caps per-slot.
- KV-sampling overhead at 1% of attention compute looked acceptable in toy run, but need a real production-run check on memory-bound instances.

End of notebook dump. Will prune and formalize into a PR/Confluence page if any of the experiments look promising after initial runs.
